problem: The company wanted to align its marketing with its environmental message.
title: Patagonia runs a Black Friday ad telling people not to buy a jacket
context: Patagonia placed a New York Times ad on Black Friday 2011 discouraging unnecessary purchases.
decision_made: Run an ad urging customers to think before buying and to repair gear.
action_taken: Published the ad and later explained its purpose and answered questions.
observed_outcome: No measured sales result for the ad was found. The only figure located was a forecast of 15 to 25 percent growth for 2011.
lessons: Claims that this ad boosted sales are often repeated without data, so treat them with caution.
limitations: Several articles mix this ad with Patagonia's 2016 Black Friday donation, which raised over $10 million. The 2011 sales effect is not documented in reliable sources found.

claims.claim_text: Patagonia ran a Black Friday 2011 ad asking customers not to buy a jacket unless they needed it.
Outside reported that Patagonia expected 2011 sales growth of 15 to 25 percent, a forecast rather than a result.
